request: Write five concise image-ad headlines for Cadian grounding sheets. The audience gets enough hours in bed but wakes tired and wants energy for the day. The sheet is a cotton and stainless-steel grounding underlay placed beneath the usual fitted sheet and connected to a properly grounded outlet. No clinical outcome evidence is supplied. Prefer curiosity and direct response. Return the headlines and one short sentence describing a suitable image.

Make one simple text-and-product image-ad concept for a desk organiser with six separate cable loops. Similar products also have six loops. No research, price or customer reviews are available. Give the headline, supporting copy, visual and CTA. Do not generate images.

Draft a concise ad and one follow-up email for a fictional mattress brand. Offer: pay $300 upfront, try for 30 nights, request a refund within that period; return collection costs $40. The enquiry came from someone asking how returns work. No health claims. Draft only, do not send.

Compare two fictional ad results from the same period. Ad A: spend $1,000, 2,000 clicks, 10 new customers. Ad B: spend $1,000, 800 clicks, 25 new customers. Each new customer's first order contributes $60 before advertising. Both ads have healthy video hook rates. No refunds or repeat purchases are recorded yet and delivery was not randomised. Explain the result and the next investigation in at most 200 words.

We have a working image ad for the six-loop desk organiser and want to find out which headline sells better. Plan a small comparison with our existing headline as the control. We have no approved budget or historical conversion volume yet. Give a usable plan and explain what we can and cannot conclude.

Suggest three names or product descriptors for a fictional cotton picnic bag with four separate compartments. No cooling, waterproofing or patented features. The brand name already exists and must stay. Explain the trade-off for each and what still needs checking.
